evidence: The diff hunk shows syncGate re-registers only the dismiss gate and leaves act untouched, so a failure on identity A would render under identity B. The agent scoped ActState.failed by identity, which fixes it without the reset the reviewer proposed. A reset in syncGate would have needed a running-state branch to avoid releasing a live child.
guidance_note: When a state value's meaning depends on another value that can change (here, the update identity), key it to that value when it is first written, not when it is reset.

evidence: The synchronous full-tree hash on the event loop is real. The agent measured it at 4-9 ms once a minute, only on source checkouts, against a 200 ms request budget, so the stall the reviewer worried about does not happen at this scale. The pushback rests on that measurement, not just on a law citation.

The packet does not include launch.ts, so it cannot confirm whether the pre-executor calls can throw. Either way the agent's choice holds: a .catch that writes 'rebuild failed: TypeError' would report an internal bug as a build failure, and the unhandledRejection path exits loudly and the daemon restarts with act idle. The round-3 reviewer re-verified that launch never rejects.

The doc says 'a bar that never shows it has it off', but updateNotice also suppresses the row when nothing is newer or the identity was dismissed, so the converse is false. The agent deleted the clause, which was one of the reviewer's two suggested fixes.
guidance_note: Before writing an if-and-only-if claim in docs, list every condition the code gates the output on and check the converse against each one.

evidence: assessBuild compares digests for equality ('digest === running.digest ? current : stale'), so 'older than the checkout's src/' misdescribes it: checking out an older commit also triggers it. The agent rewrote the doc as an identity check and gave a reasoned case for keeping the 'Newer source' label.
guidance_note: When documenting a check, describe the comparison the code actually performs (equality or ordering), not the motivating scenario.

evidence: The agent argues the not-source-checkout return comes before every fallible step in assessBuild (a constant entryUrl, path arithmetic, and existsSync, which never throws), so a published install cannot first sample as unchecked. The packet does not show assessBuild's body to confirm this. The round-3 reviewer independently accepted it as a daemon-lifetime constant.

guidance_note: When a feature's payoff is an effect such as a self-restart, write the e2e test for the success path in the original PR, not only the failure path.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the original PR added updateNotice to the fixture without asserting on it, and c9dd07c did not touch this test. c9ec4c1 adds not.toHaveProperty checks for updateNotice and separator and renames the test.
guidance_note: When adding a field to a fixture in an 'every field' test, add the assertion for that field too, including a negative assertion if the field is deliberately not projected.

guidance_note: When a fix changes a contract that the finding itself quoted from a doc, grep for that quoted phrase and update every occurrence in the same commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the applyUpdate verb handler is original-PR code that c9dd07c did not change, and no test dispatched it. The added daemon-click test takes the real handler from VERBS and covers a valid session id, an empty one, and '../etc'.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: c9ec4c1 added a source-arm success test, and the reviewer only uses it for contrast. The release arm has had no e2e click-through since the original PR. narrative: Round 0 found a real identity-scoping gap (F1), which the agent fixed by putting the identity on the data, plus two doc inaccuracies and two pushbacks that held up. The one fix-caused finding is F9: CLAUDE.md kept the 'until the next attempt' wording that F1 had quoted. Rounds 2 and 3 were otherwise test-coverage gaps from the original PR, which the post-review flags misattribute to a formatting-only commit.
guidance_observations: The agent backed pushbacks with measurements (F2's digest timing) or code traces (F6), not just law tokens, and every pushback survived the next round.
Test coverage of the success path and the verb dispatch was left for the reviewer to request; writing those tests in the original PR would have removed most of round 2.

evidence: Every fixture's DFLT.root had no when, so the path where a rows-merge inherits base.when was never exercised. 0793b9d adds the test 'rows: a fragment without `when` keeps the base's `when`'.
guidance_note: When writing merge tests, cover each field in all three states: inherited, overridden, and absent on both sides.

evidence: The original restages returned '!isRowsFragment || rows.length > 0', so '{ rows: {}, when }' counted as the identity even though it gates the bar. 0793b9d adds the when check and tests the presetRoot path.
guidance_note: When defining 'is the identity of this merge', derive the predicate from every field the merge carries, not just the main collection.

evidence: GROUP_NAME_RE redefined the same regex as ROW_NAME_RE, and ROW_NAME_RE's comment said the two share the constraint. 0793b9d deletes GROUP_NAME_RE and uses ROW_NAME_RE.
guidance_note: When a comment says a constant is 'shared with X', check that X actually imports it.

evidence: The anchor-count check over presetRoot's merged tree was new behavior, and its own comment named the cross-row case as newly possible, but nothing tested it. 0793b9d adds a settings-menu test expecting a ConfigError at presets.wide.root.
guidance_note: When a comment says a scenario is newly possible, write the test for that scenario in the same commit.

evidence: Merging by name lets a file row re-place charsetControl alongside the inherited identity row, and the per-file walk in menu-synth cannot see that. 0793b9d moves the check into cross-ref over the rendered trees, and a test confirms the ConfigError.

evidence: The diff deletes the horizontal wrapper around a bare-segment root, so the chrome splices as vertical siblings. The agent did not restore the root-only wrap the reviewer asked for. Instead it treated every segment child of a vertical container as a one-cell row. Its test fails at 5 lines versus 2 without the fix.
guidance_note: When deleting a special-case branch during a refactor, write a test that pins the behavior that branch existed for before deleting it.

evidence: The RenderCache fixtures only authored whole-tree roots. The 0793b9d test writes a rows file and asserts both the merged keys and the authoredRoots flip, though it drops the plan's 'reload back clears it' step.
guidance_note: When adding a new authoring surface, add one end-to-end test through the real file-and-reload path in the original PR.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: rowsSpec's hardcoded findKeyLine(ctx.source, ['root']) is original-PR code that 0793b9d did not touch. Its use for preset fragments gave wrong line numbers. 8804a82 derives the line from path, and a test confirms the preset line.
guidance_note: When a FieldSpec receives a path argument, derive every diagnostic's line from that path and copy the existing path-aware pattern (groupLabelSpec) rather than hardcoding one call site.

evidence: The F2 fix (0793b9d) created the presetRoot describe block and pinned only the identity and when-only arms of restages, leaving the ordinary non-empty-rows arm untested there. 8804a82 adds that case.
guidance_note: When a fix rewrites a predicate with N disjuncts, add one test per disjunct, not only the one the finding named.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: layoutPlacementOf returned only layer.path and the splice re-searched in file-text order in the original PR, and 0793b9d did not touch config-file-store. 8804a82 stamps the row address into each cascade entry. Its test fails without the fix by editing extra instead of identity.
guidance_note: When one function resolves a target and another acts on it, pass the resolved address itself, not a coarser key that the second function has to search again.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the hardcoded 'presets.${preset}.root' error string is original-PR code. 8804a82 names stagedPathOf, which it shares with resetPathOf.
The F5 fix (0793b9d) added the menu-host branch to checkPlacementCounts, which runs at both the top level and per preset, but tested only the top-level call. 8804a82 adds the preset-scoped test.
guidance_note: When moving a check into a function that is called from several sites, test the moved check from each call site.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 8804a82 did not touch cross-ref.ts, and the hardcoded presetKey sits in the original-PR hunk. A '{ rows: {} }' preset re-walks the root tree and reports a duplicate issue under the wrong path. d0b17bd keys the census by presetRoot(cfg, name).path.
guidance_note: When a function already returns 'where this is authored' (presetRoot.path), use that value for diagnostics instead of rebuilding the path string.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the schema's ROOT_FRAGMENT_REF is original-PR code, and the ajv-versus-loader corpora never included a rows root. d0b17bd adds good and bad rows cases.
guidance_note: When adding a new schema shape, add it to the existing schema-conformance corpora in the same PR.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the walkNodes(fragmentNode(out.root)) line comes from the original PR. 0793b9d only removed the placement counting beside it. d0b17bd adds a test with a menu in a row's when.

The flag is a false positive: 8804a82 only extracted stagedPathOf from resetPathOf's existing 'presetLayer(doc, ...)?.path ?? [root]' and reused it in the error message. The declaration-existence criterion and its 'same fact presetRoot projects' comment predate the fix. d0b17bd adds restagesFragment so presetLayer uses the same classification as presetRoot.

evidence: This duplicates F13: the hardcoded presetKey comes from the original-PR cross-ref hunk, and 8804a82 did not touch cross-ref.ts, so the flag is a false positive. It is fixed by the same d0b17bd change that keys the census by presetRoot path.

narrative: This is a large refactor from tree root to named rows. Round 0 found real bugs: restages ignored when, the menu-host placement check ran per file, and the bare-segment chrome stacked vertically. Every fix was sound. Two round-1 findings were coverage gaps in those fixes' own tests (F9, F12). Most ON-NAMED-FIX flags are false positives on original-PR code. Each round was carried by findings independent of earlier fixes, so no round is attributable to an incomplete fix.
guidance_observations: The agent repeatedly extended fixes one level more generally than the reviewer asked (F6 covers any vertical parent; F10 stamps the address into the cascade), and none of them drew regressions.
Several findings were 'two computations of the same fact disagree' (F13, F16, F17); a pre-review sweep for duplicated classifications would have caught them before review.

evidence: '(indexOf + depth) % length' with a negative depth does produce index -1, but the only producer is the literal BAR_DEPTH = 0, and the planned producer is a list length, which is non-negative. The reviewer admits it is unreachable. The agent recorded the real constraint (the ai7.9 derivation must be a length) on the ticket that will write the producer.

narrative: There was one round with a single advisory about negative depth in hueAtDepth. The agent pushed back with a producer-based argument and moved the remaining risk onto the ticket that will introduce non-zero depths. Nothing was fix-caused.
guidance_observations: Routing a valid future-risk concern to the ticket that writes the risky producer, instead of adding a guard now, kept the PR at one round.

evidence: render.ts's header still said '+ the hue counter' after the PR deleted that mechanism. 6ecd9cf drops the clause from both headers. The verification grep was the literal 'hue counter', which F6 shows was too narrow.
guidance_note: When deleting a mechanism, grep for every name and synonym it went by (hue shift, rotation, cursor, step, counter) before opening the PR.

evidence: This duplicates F1 for node-registry.ts's header, and the 6ecd9cf diff shows the clause removed.
This duplicates F1 for the same render.ts line, and 6ecd9cf removes it.

This duplicates F2. The header contradicted the tint-by-address lines the same PR added below it, and 6ecd9cf fixes it by deleting the clause.

6ecd9cf did not touch segment-color.ts. The stale 'per-segment hue rotation' sentence was left by the original PR, and the F1 fix's literal grep for 'hue counter' missed it, as the reviewer notes. 656d3a3 swept the whole class and found five more siblings.
guidance_note: When fixing one stale reference to a deleted mechanism, sweep for the concept under all its names, not the literal phrase in the finding; the later sweep found five more.

narrative: Round 0 raised five duplicate stale-comment findings about the deleted hue counter. The agent fixed them with a grep for the literal 'hue counter'. Round 1 found a sibling under different wording (F6). The class-wide sweep then fixed five more, so round 2 was only needed to verify it. The round summaries also flag CLAUDE.md:126 and interaction-authoring.md:1367 as still stale after merge; the agent's sweep covered only src/.
guidance_observations: A deletion PR should finish with a synonym sweep across src/ and docs/. The round-2 summary shows two doc passages still describing the deleted mechanism at merge.

evidence: rootOf destructured only when and rootNode re-attached only when, so a whole-tree root's distribution was dropped. Instead of adding distribution to both functions, the agent derived Root from ContainerOwn and rest-spread the fields, so any future container field also crosses.
guidance_note: When adding a field to a node type, grep every place that hand-lists that type's fields (here, 'when !== undefined && { when }') and convert each to a derived or rest-spread form in the same PR.

evidence: The F1 fix (3d37e77) converted authoredFragment to a rest-spread, but the authoredLayout container case directly above it still hand-picked when and dropped distribution on nested containers. 77500e0 rest-spreads it too, and a test confirms the round-trip is lossless.
guidance_note: When a fix converts one hand-listed field copy to a rest-spread, grep the 'when !== undefined && { when }' pattern across the repo and convert or justify every hit in the same commit.

evidence:
3d37e77 made '{ rows: {}, distribution }' legal and generalized restages, but the json5 twin restagesFragment still checked only rows and when. A reset would then delete the top-level root instead of presets.

.root. 77500e0 aligns the twin, and an integration test fails on the pre-fix predicate.
guidance_note: When changing a predicate that has a documented twin on another substrate, update both in the same commit and add a test that feeds both the same inputs.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 3d37e77 did not touch decor.test.ts, and the uniform-vdc address comes from the original PR. The added heterogeneous test selects entry 9, which differs from both uniform folds (5 and 8).
guidance_note: When a function changes from one global parameter to a per-element parameter, add a unit test where the elements differ, so a fold that reuses one value fails.

evidence: The F1 fix's rest-spread pattern needed ignoreRestSiblings, and the reviewer itself confirmed it was necessary. The repo-wide scope is a real trade-off, but a name listed beside ...rest is an intentional omission, so the pushback is sound.

narrative: Round 0 found a real silent drop of distribution on the whole-tree root. The agent fixed it in the type, which was the right shape, but the sweep stopped at root.ts and authoredFragment. Round 1 found the sibling hand-picked copy in authoredLayout (F2) and the restagesFragment twin that 209/F16 had introduced (F3). Round 2 was clean but would have run anyway for F4's independent test fix.
guidance_observations: The F1 fix converted the field-copy idiom in some places but did not grep for the remaining instances. Two of round 1's three actionable findings were those leftover instances.

restagesFragment was created as a twin of restages in PR 209 (F16), and here the twins drifted on the first predicate change. A twin that is kept in sync by comments alone is a recurring source of findings.
